messages.subject: Known issues
messages.body_plain:
raster 3.0-7

Newer versions of raster have broken something in projection() and projection()<-. I am currently working on a fix. For the moment, it looks like everything works fine if you don't have the raster package loaded.

ctmm 0.5.5

occurrence() has a bug that distorts the density estimate if the mean location is far from the origin of the coordinate system. This bug is fixed in version 0.5.6.

ctmm 0.5.3 & 0.5.4

Step-wise model selection in ctmm.select() can proceed from OUF to the new OUf/OUO models introduced in 0.5.3 and terminate without attempting an OU model, even though an OU/IID model should ultimately be selected. This behavior is counter intuitive, because the OUf/OUO models are more autocorrelated than the OUF model and the OU model is less autocorrelated, but this does happen with real data. This issue is fixed in ctmm 0.5.4.

But, in pushing out the quick fix to 0.5.3's ctmm.select() bug, I slipped in a different bug to summary() to where all CIs on model-fit timescales are reported to run from 0 to infinity. The model fits are actually fine. The bug is isolated to summary()'s timescale CIs when applied to model fits. This issue is fixed in ctmm 0.5.5.

ctmm 0.5.10+

An update in either R package manipulate or RStudio has caused manipulate functions like zoom() and ctmm.guess() to be unreliable on some systems. I have not been able to successfully isolate this behavior. Running the functions multiple times often works.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
  I am in the early phases of beginning an analysis to look at overlap in home ranges of a brown bear population. I read the Winner et al. 2018 paper ("Statistical inference for home range overlap") and would like to use the methodology described in the paper. However, when I was going through the accompanying R script, I encountered an error:

Error in overlap(data.tm <http://data.tm>, models, weights = TRUE, debias = TRUE) :telemetry object class not supported by overlap.

I then read in the ctmm change logs that "overlap() telemetry and CTMM arguments depreciated" for 0.5.2.

My question is then, how to compute the overlap ala

### COMPUTE THE OVERLAP BETWEEN EACH PAIR OF ANIMALS ###

cat("Computing overlap of all pairs\n")
overlap.CIs <- overlap(data.tm <http://data.tm>, models, weights=TRUE, debias=TRUE)

as shown in the Winner et al. 2018 R script?

Because I am not super fluent in R, I was hoping to be able to follow and modify the accompanying script as much as possible. Any help or assistance you could provide would be greatly appreciated!

Regards,
Jenny Hansen

messages.subject: Issues with as.telemetry() from move object
messages.subject_clean: Issues with as.telemetry() from move object
messages.body_plain:
We are working with a large multi-year data set of GPS relocations of tortoises. My current issue is coercing our data into a telemetry object from a move object. I can make the move object for an individual animal with no issue, but when I use "as.telemetry" to coerce into a telemetry object I get thousands of lines that say "Minimum sampling interval of Inf years in XXXXX" and warnings:
"1: In Move2CSV(object, timeformat = timeformat, timezone = timezone,  ... :Move objects in geographic coordinates are automatically projected."
and "In min(dt) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf"
 and the resulting object can't used in any further functions.

This is the code I am using (allgps is a SpatialPointsDataFrame pulled from our Postgres server):

allgps$DateTime <- as.POSIXct(allgps$DateTime, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

allgps.df <- as.data.frame(allgps)

CN802.a<-allgps.df[allgps.df$Tort == "CN802",]
CN802.a <- CN802.a[order(CN802.a$DateTime),]

CN802.a.m <- move(x=CN802.a$x, y=CN802.a$y,time=CN802.a$DateTime, data=CN802.a, proj=proj4string(allgps),sensor="gps", animal=CN802.a$Tort)
CN802.a.t <- as.telemetry(CN802.a.m, timeformat="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", timezone= "America/Los_Angeles",timeout=Inf,na.rm="row", drop=TRUE)

What's strange is that my colleague also used this same code to get a subset of this data to work fine, the only differences I can find between our approaches is that she started from a .csv which she had edited in Excel, but I can't find any differences between the structure of her move object and mine.

I found that can run the move object through the functions here: https://rpubs.com/dracodoc/252699
and get a telemetry object, though I then get errors about UERE missing when I try to go use ctmm.fit()

I'm assuming it has something to do with POSIX formatting, but I am at a bit of a loss now,

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Hi Jenny,

There is an example in help("overlap"), but if data.tm <http://data.tm> is the list of telemetry objects and models is the corresponding list of model fits, then

AKDES <- akde(data.tm <http://data.tm>,models) # put weights=TRUE here if you need to

would give a corresponding list of AKDEs, all calculated on the same grid, and

overlap.CIs <- overlap(AKDES)

would finish the calculation.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Issues with as.telemetry() from move object
messages.subject_clean: Issues with as.telemetry() from move object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Steve,

This sounds like problems with the timestamp format or timezone. I can point out a couple of things:

You could be feeding in different timestamps into move() and as.telemetry(). For move() you did not supply a timezone argument in as.POSIXct(), which means that the (default) local timezone of your computer was used. Yet for as.telemetry(), you supplied the timezone of "America/Los_Angeles". I would also note, that most collars/tags are UTC, to avoid timezone issues, and not the timezone of the study area.
When you open and re-save a CSV file in Excel, it can reformat your timestamps. Usually this is a danger because it can corrupt your data, but in this case it could have served to fix or better standardize your timestamps.
If that doesn't fix your problems, then you can feel free to send me some sample data to replicate the issue and I can take a look.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.subject_clean: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for your help earlier. I have a bit of an update on my end. Two things:

1. Copy/pasting my error info from sigloc into the telemetry object as COV.x.x, etc. seemed to work, but I'm not really seeing any difference between home ranges with and without errors. This could be because the errors are so large relative to where the points are located to eachother. I did encounter one error when trying to plot location data (with error = 1):

Error in pracma::ellipke(sqrt(1 - B2)) :
  Some elements of argument 'm' are out of range.

The result was a blank plot. I think it's because some of my errors are relatively large compared to others (like an order of magnitude or two, from 80m --> 4000m); they are also large on points very close together. When I removed those points from the dataset I no longer encountered the error, and it plotted with error ellipses - however in some cases this did not work.

I've attached code and some sample data.

2. I'm trying to brainstorm how to get error "ellipses" from the ATM/razimuth package into ctmm. The razimuth output isn't as easy as the copy/paste from sigloc. The advantage for me is that I get associated error with locations that the package sigloc was unable to find a maximum likelihood estimate for, and kind of a likelihood density plot associated with each point instead of just ellipses.

Is there any chance you've given more thought into incorporating ATM error "ellipses" into ctmm?

I've also attached some code and sample data which should give an example of razimuth output, if you are interested.

Cheers,

Chris

messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.subject_clean: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

It looks like you did not turn error on in the model guess before fitting. Error is off by default. See the error vignette: https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/error.html

Some of those COV values have very impossible values, which imply negative variances along one axis. I can fix the plot function to handle small errors, but those are relatively large.

If you have a probability density, then from that you can either calculate the mean location & covariance matrix or you can calculate the mode & local curvature to construct the error ellipses.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Modify Winner et al 2018 R script to calculate AKDE overlap
messages.subject_clean: Modify Winner et al 2018 R script to calculate AKDE overlap
messages.body_plain:
Here's the code from Winner et al. 2018, modified to run on the buffalo dataset from the package:

library(ctmm)

### DATA PREPARATION ###

# load the buffalo data from ctmm
# this dataset consists of observations of 6 individual animals
data("buffalo")
data.tm <http://data.tm>  <- buffalo
n.indivs <- length(data.tm <http://data.tm>)

### IDENTIFICATION OF RANGE-RESIDENT SUBPOPULATION ###

# visually inspect each trajectory for evidence of range-resident (rr) behavior
rr <- vector("character")
for(i.indiv in seq(1, n.indivs)) {
  indiv.id <http://indiv.id> <- data.tm <http://data.tm>[[i.indiv]]@info$identity

  par(mfrow=c(1,2))
  # note: layering the movement over satellite imagery can be very helpful
  #       but is not done here

  # plot the raw movement data
  plot(data.tm <http://data.tm>[[i.indiv]], type='l',
       main=indiv.id <http://indiv.id>)

  # plot the variogram
  # for additional information on how to interpret variograms see
  # vignette("variogram", package="ctmm")
  SVF = variogram(data.tm <http://data.tm>[[i.indiv]])
  plot(SVF, fraction=0.5, level=c(0.5, 0.95))

  # read a single character ('y' means accept as rr, else reject)
  decision <- readline(prompt = sprintf("Is %s rr? y/(n): ", indiv.id <http://indiv.id>))
  if(decision == 'y')
    rr <- c(rr, indiv.id <http://indiv.id>)
}

# in the experiments we present, we selected the following 6 animals as rr:
rr <- c("Cilla"  "Gabs"   "Mvubu"  "Pepper" "Queen"  "Toni")

# remove non-range resident individuals
data.tm <http://data.tm>  <- data.tm <http://data.tm>[sapply(data.tm <http://data.tm>, function(t) t@info$identity) %in% rr]
n.indivs <- length(data.tm <http://data.tm>)

### FIT A MOVEMENT MODEL TO EACH INDIVIDUAL ###

models <- list()
for(i.indiv in seq(1, n.indivs)) {
  indiv.id <http://indiv.id> <- data.tm <http://data.tm>[[i.indiv]]@info$identity
  cat(sprintf("Fitting model for %s\n", indiv.id <http://indiv.id>))

  # start with a reasonable initial guess
  guess <- ctmm.guess(data.tm <http://data.tm>[[i.indiv]], interactive=FALSE)

  FITS <- ctmm.select(data.tm <http://data.tm>[[i.indiv]],
                      CTMM    = guess,
                      verbose = TRUE,
                      level   = 1,
                      method  = "pHREML",
                      control=list(method="pNewton",cores = -1),
                      trace = TRUE)

  # store the model with the lowest AICc
  if(class(FITS) == "list") {models[[indiv.id <http://indiv.id>]] <- FITS[[1]]} else {

    models[[indiv.id <http://indiv.id>]] <- FITS
  }
}

### ESTIMATE THE HR AREAS OF THE RR INDIVIDUALS ON THE SAME GRID

cat("Estimating HR areas of all rr individuals \n")
UDs <- akde(data.tm <http://data.tm>, models) #use weights = TRUE if necessary

### COMPUTE THE OVERLAP BETWEEN EACH PAIR OF ANIMALS ###

cat("Computing overlap of all pairs\n")

overlap.CIs <- overlap(UDs)

### ANALYSIS ###

## example 1 ##
# list each pair of individuals and the three CI components
ut <- upper.tri(overlap.CIs[,,1], diag=FALSE)
overlap.df <- data.frame(i=rep(rownames(overlap.CIs),
                               ncol(overlap.CIs))[as.vector(ut)],
                         j=rep(colnames(overlap.CIs),
                               each=nrow(overlap.CIs))[as.vector(ut)],
                         lower=overlap.CIs[,,1][ut],
                         ml   =overlap.CIs[,,2][ut],
                         upper=overlap.CIs[,,3][ut])

# find a pair where the CI includes 0.01 and one that is above 0.01
example.weak   <- Position(function(x) x < 0.01, overlap.df$lower)
example.strong <- Position(function(x) x > 0.01, overlap.df$lower)

ids.weak   <- c(toString(overlap.df[example.weak,'i']),
                toString(overlap.df[example.weak,'j']))
ids.strong <- c(toString(overlap.df[example.strong,'i']),
                toString(overlap.df[example.strong,'j']))

# compute the UDs for each pair
data.weak   <- data.tm <http://data.tm>[ids.weak]
data.strong <- data.tm <http://data.tm>[ids.strong]
models.weak   <- models[ids.weak]
models.strong <- models[ids.strong]
UDs.weak   <- akde(data.weak,   models.weak,   weights = TRUE)
UDs.strong <- akde(data.strong, models.strong, weights = TRUE)

# plot the UDs of each example
col <- c("red", "blue")
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(data.weak, UD=UDs.weak,
     main=sprintf("{%s,%s}: BC = (%.3f, %.3f, %.3f)",
                  ids.weak[1], ids.weak[2],

messages.subject: Re: AKDE for a herd
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robert,

I would avoid that route and instead try to add spatially constraining terms to the model, as is done in "synoptic" home-range estimation. This effectively adds a smooth notion of availability (really, it is site fidelity now) that is fit to the data simultaneously with the covariate dependence, instead of a (typically) discontinuous spatial constraint that is chosen a priori. Also, fitting the spatial dependence first, as is typically done with MCP->RSF, doesn't allow the model to completely tease apart the two influences, and so robs the covariates of some of their explanatory power.

Just make sure your data satisfies the IID assumptions when doing RSFs. If you need to thin the data but want to use all of the data, then you can run all possible coarsenings of the data and average the results together (without shrinking the standard errors).

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Aloha,

I am trying to learn how to use the ctmm package for my thesis by creating the kernel densities for home range analysis. My data was collected using automated telemetry towers, but I am located in Hawaii where we use UTM rather than lat long. The data does not belong to me and I have been told not to upload it to Movebank as it will be made public later. I am having issues getting the data correctly formatted so it will import correctly. My column headers are band.num (bird ID ex: 93229899), date (1/17/18), time (11:30 - using military time), UTM East (251402.412), and UTM North (2174029.523).

I think part of the reason I am getting so many errors is the UTM and date and time formats, but everything I try with as.POSIXct and as.telemetry is not working. Do you have any advice?

Thank you,
Erin

messages.subject: Re: data import - UTM?
messages.body_plain:
Aloha Erin,

I've just put support for importing UTM coordinates in the development branch, which you can install via devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm") . Otherwise you can inverse project from UTM to long-lat with rgdal::project().

You will need a column designating the UTM zone.

You will need to rename band.num to a Movebank attribute like animal.ID or individual.local.identifier. I can add support for band.num in the future.

You will need to paste() the date and time together into one timestamp column. You might also need to provide a time format argument if as.POSIXct() can not automatically figure out your timestamp format.

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/as.telemetry.html

https://www.movebank.org/node/2381

Best,
Chris
